title: awinut
The Tradition of Cursing Imam Ali from the Pulpits (Sabb) and Hujr b. Adi
hook: Imam Ali was cursed from the pulpits; Hujr b. Adi, who refused to curse him, was killed.
scenes.0.text: After the reconciliation of **Hasan**, from the 41st year of the Hijrah, on the order of Mu'awiya, the curse of **Ali** was pronounced on all minbars under his rule. This was not the work of a governor or a city alone. Mu'awiya himself ordered his governors not to stop cursing Ali, and he made them do it. The Friday sermons were opened with insults to the Prophet's uncle and son-in-law. This practice was performed in the largest mosques of the cities, in front of large crowds. The Prophet said, "He who loves Ali loves me. He who kisses Ali kisses me". But Mu'awiya's administration had begun to criminalize love for the Ahl al-Bayt. Those who loved Ali had to listen in silence every Friday to the insults he hurled at the man they loved the most.
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: 1inzbgl
Mu'awiya
scenes.1.text: Kufa was the capital during the caliphate of Ali and was the most populous city of his lovers. Mu'awiya ordered the governor of Kufa, Mu'awer b. Shu'bah, to continue to malign Ali. In his sermons, Muğire insulted both Ali and those who loved him. **Ziyad**, who became governor of Kufa after Mu'awiya, continued the same oppression with even greater severity. The governors announced this curse from the pulpit to the whole nation. The congregation at Friday prayers heard a curse read to the Prophet's closest relative instead of saying amen.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: 14t0drj
Mughira
scenes.2.text: One day Mu'awiya asked Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, "What prevented you from cursing Abu Turab?" Abu Turab was a lovely nickname given to Ali by the Prophet. Sa'd recalled three words the Prophet said about Ali. The first was the hadith of Manzile, which was recited in Tebek. The second was to give the flag in Khyber to anyone who loved Allah and His Messenger. The third was that the Prophet took Ali and his family with him on the day of Mubahala. Sa'd said that he would never insult Ali for hearing these words. This conversation is going to be on Muslim.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 2d5wgv
Sa'd b. Abi Waqqas
scenes.2.art.actors.1.label: 1inzbgl
Mu'awiya
scenes.3.text: The governor sent a general to all the governors. A general is an official order written to the governors. In this order, he demanded that Ali be insulted, and that those who praised and loved him be punished. Those who spoke of Ali's virtues were declared enemies of the state. Those who loved the Ahl al-Bayt had to hide their love. Even in the homes, the name of 'Ali was whispered. The love of the Prophet's family became a secret at the cost of his life in the land of the Emvi.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 1inzbgl
Mu'awiya
scenes.4.text: According to Ahl al-Bayt, Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, heard about this curse and wrote a letter to Mu'awiya and the governors. In his letter, he recalled the Prophet's words: "Whoever insults Ali insults me". So the curse that was pronounced on Ali in the pulpits was actually on the Prophet himself. Umm Salamah, as one of the wives of the Prophet, thought it her duty to speak about it. But the Deputy ignored that warning. The letter was read, but the curse in the sermons didn't change.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: 12fi29o
Umm Salama
scenes.4.art.actors.1.label: 1inzbgl
Mu'awiya
scenes.5.text: He was a v**aliant** commander who fought alongside **Hucr b. Adi** in Kufa, Jameel and Siffin. On a Friday, when the governor Muğire was cursing Ali in his sermon, Hucr couldn't stand it and stood up. He said aloud that Ali's virtue was far superior to that of his detractors. Then Ziad, the governor of the Kufa, seized the Hujr. Hucr and about twelve of his companions were taken to Damascus. His only crime was not accepting the curse read from the pulpit.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: 5dbya0
Hujr b. Adi
scenes.6.text: **Hucr** and his companions, who were taken to Damascus, were asked to curse Ali and tell him that they had distanced themselves from him. Hujr and those who resisted with him denied it. In the year 51 of the Hijrah, ==they were slaughtered== at a place called Merju Azra on the road to Damascus. He said he knew he was going to be martyred after the prayer. The Mu'awiya defended this blood against those who challenged him for this massacre. Hucr and his companions were killed because they refused to curse Ali. The last prayer of the Hujr was this two rak'ahs prayer.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: 5dbya0
Hujr b. Adi
scenes.7.text: According to Ahl-i-Bait, the curse on the minbars lasted for about 60 years. The practice began in the 41st year of the Hijrah and continued until 99-101. This time is not given as an exact number but as an approximation. Umar b. Every Friday, the name of **Ali** was mentioned in the pulpits as an insult until Abdulaziz removed this practice. Children born and raised in those years grew up listening to the curse of the Prophet recited to the nearest one during Friday prayers. A generation has known Ali by hearing this curse.
scenes.7.art.actors.1.label: 1skmpdf
Preacher
scenes.8.text: When Umar b. Abdulaziz became caliph, he lifted the curse. He's sent letters to all the municipalities ordering the application to be stopped. In the sermons, the curse was replaced by verse 90 of Surah Nahl: "Allah commands justice, kindness, and giving to the near of kin. He forbids indecency and wickedness and oppression". Nearly sixty years of persecution thus ended. The curse of Ali was no longer recited in the pulpits. But the wounds of the years were not easily healed, and those who loved the Ahl-i-Bait never forgot those years.
scenes.8.art.actors.0.label: xt2qi8
Umar b. Abd al-Aziz
sunni.0.says: From Sa'd b. Abi Waqqas, narrated by his son Amir b. Sa'd: Mu'awiya asked Sa'd why he did not curse Abu Turab (Imam Ali); Sa'd stated that he would not curse him, listing three sayings of the Prophet about Ali. The wording "Manzila" about Ali also appears in this narration.
sunni.1.says: Mughira b. Shu'ba, following Mu'awiya's advice, cursing Ali and his supporters in the Friday sermons; Hujr's reaction; Ziyad's arrest; the execution at Marj Adhra of those who refused to curse Ali (d. 51/671); Aisha's disapproval.
sunni.2.says: Umar b. Abd al-Aziz ended the practice of cursing Ali in the sermons; he returned Fadak to the Ahl al-Bayt. It does not mention the verse Nahl 90.
sunni.3.says: Mu'awiya's advice to Mughira to speak ill of Ali and praise Uthman; the Hujr b. Adi incident.
sunni.4.says: The insult during the Muğire and the Ziyad and the Hucr b. The story of Adi's murder is expected.
sunni.5.says: Transmission concerning Mervan's abuse of Ali during the governorship of Medina (source cited by WikiShia as a Sunni historian).
sunni.6.says: From Umm Salamah, a saying that insulting Ali is considered insulting the Prophet. WikiShia gives this with Ibn Asâkir (Tarihu Damask 42/533).
sunni.7.says: The alleged letter from Umm Salamah to Mu'awiya: "You insult Allah and His Messenger on your benches".
sunni.8.says: That Umar b. Abd al-Aziz wrote to all the Islamic provinces ordering the curse to be stopped.
sunni.9.says: It's a common narrative to read Nahl 90 instead of swearing.
sunni.10.says: Transmissions about the habit of swearing in the minbars and the location of the Hucr.
shia.0.says: General messages from Mu'awiya to the governors: punishment of those who narrate the virtues of Ali, insulting him in the sermons. page unclear.
shia.1.says: That the practice lasted about sixty years (a sentence without a footnote), its prohibition by Umar b. Abd al-Aziz (Ibn Khaldun vol. 3 p. 94), Mughira's cursing throughout nine years of governorship (Baladhuri, Ansab vol. 5 p. 243), the Umm Salama hadith (Ibn Tawus; Ibn Asakir 42/533), Majlisi, Bihar al-Anwar 39/311-330.
shia.2.says: That when Hujr and Amr b. al-Hamiq cursed the people of Damascus at Siffin, Ali forbade it, saying "I do not like your cursing"; Ali did not tolerate cursing even on his own side.
shia.3.says: These sources are supposed to be talking about the Hucr incident and the abuse.
disputes.0.title: 1tob7bn
Was the cursing a direct order?
disputes.0.shia: That Ali was cursed from the pulpits is recounted in both traditions. Shia sources link this to the circulars Mu'awiya wrote to his governors.
disputes.0.sunni: That Ali was cursed from the pulpits is recounted in both traditions. Tabari mentions it as a recommendation to Mughira; some commentators read Muslim 2404 as a question, not an order.
disputes.1.title: 15maz35
How many years did the tradition last?
disputes.1.shia: It is accepted that the practice lasted until Umar b. Abd al-Aziz. The phrase "about sixty years" appears in Shia publications and has no footnote.
disputes.1.sunni: The app's called Umar b. It's accepted that he drove to Abdelaziz. The number "sixty" is not based on a classic Sunni text; it is also disputed that it is celebrated every Friday everywhere.
disputes.2.title: wl9tse
To which cities did the cursing spread?
disputes.2.shia: That the cursing was practiced in Kufa is agreed. In the Shia account, this includes Damascus, Basra and Medina as well; those who objected were punished.
disputes.2.sunni: That the cursing was practiced in Kufa is agreed. Sunni examples are given mostly through Mughira, Ziyad and Marwan; whether it was to the same extent in the Hijaz and Egypt is uncertain.
disputes.3.title: en9i24
Why was Hujr killed?
disputes.3.shia: That Hujr was killed at Marj Adhra is common ground in the sources. In the Shia account, he is a martyr because he refused to curse Ali.
disputes.3.sunni: That Hujr was killed at Marj Adhra is common ground in the sources. Historians also mention his actions regarded as rebellion against Ziyad; Aisha criticized this killing.
disputes.4.title: uwvpmx
The verse Umar b. Abd al-Aziz had recited
disputes.4.shia: That Umar b. Abd al-Aziz abolished the cursing is recounted in both traditions. Nahl 90 is mentioned in Shia accounts as the verse recited in its place.
disputes.4.sunni: Umar b. It's told in both traditions that Abdulaziz abolished the curse. The recitation of Nahl 90 is a common narrative; it is not based on a primary text, which verse was first recited when.
questions.0: Umm Salamah wrote a letter reminding her of the Prophet's words: "He who insults Ali insults me". Why, do you think, did the Deputy continue to abuse the word despite this warning?
questions.1: Sa'd told Mu'awiya of the three sayings of the Prophet about Ali: the range, the banner of Khaybar and the Mubahele. Why do you think Sa'd chose those three words as his reason for refusing to swear?
questions.2: Ali had forbidden his own soldiers to curse at the other side. Why do you think Mu'awiya turned the same insult into a government order?
questions.3: Hucr and his friends were killed because they refused to swear. Why do you think the Mu'awiya government has retaliated with death for those who refused to blaspheme?
questions.4: Umar b. Abdul Aziz lifted the curse and recited verse 90 of Surah Nahl instead. Do you think Umar b. Why didn't Abdul Aziz just lift the curse and recite the verse of justice in the sermon?
summary: In the Umayyad period, Ali was cursed in the Friday sermons. Hujr b. Adi, who refused to curse, was killed at Marj Adhra in 51 H. Umar b. Abd al-Aziz abolished the practice. In the Shia account, this is a grave injustice that lasted about sixty years.
notes.0: After the peace of Hasan (41 H), authority was consolidated in Mu'awiya.
notes.1: In the Umayyad period, cursing Ali in the sermons became an established practice.
notes.2: In Muslim 2404, Mu'awiya asks Sa'd why he does not curse Ali.
notes.3: Hujr b. Adi was killed at Marj Adhra in 51 H because he refused to curse.
notes.4: Umar b. Abd al-Aziz abolished this practice.
